personality_voice.book_baseline: Across all seven books, Hagrid's voice is one of the most consistent in the series: broad West Country dialect with dropped consonants and contracted words, emotional transparency (he cries, roars, and jokes in rapid succession), warm protectiveness, guileless secret-spilling, creature enthusiasm, and a capacity for wounded pride and quick anger. He is simultaneously gentle and physically imposing, sentimental and oblivious, fiercely loyal and chronically self-sabotaging. His voice is among the most distinctive in the corpus.
personality_voice.film_portrayal: Robbie Coltrane preserves the dialect, the emotional openness, the protectiveness, and the warmth across all films with consistent fidelity. The core personality pattern - warm bluster, tearful grief, creature enthusiasm, guileless over-explanation - is present in every film appearance. High-fidelity moments include the betrayal monologue in DH Part 1, the spider-hint scene in CoS, the pre-execution scene in PoA, and the Aragog burial in HBP.
personality_voice.difference: The film series consistently loses secondary personality texture: the extended sulking wounded-pride cycles (HBP), the self-deprecating political opinions (PS), the specific sharp humor (Lockhart dismissal in CoS, the Ginny wink), the Azkaban trauma confession (PoA, the single deepest interiority moment in the corpus), the flobberworm confidence-collapse phase (PoA), and the drunk-alone vulnerability (PoA). The added 'storm coming' line in OotP is a minor off-note. Across books, the films favor the warmer, more immediately sympathetic Hagrid over the one who is also petty, oblivious, politically naive, and capable of self-destructive stubbornness.
personality_voice.evidence_status: Directly evidenced across all seven per-book analyses
personality_voice.penalty_logic: The dominant personality is strongly and consistently preserved. No film introduces traits that distort or contradict the book character. The losses are cumulative texture rather than fundamental misrepresentation - the same pattern of minor simplification repeating across every book. Books 1-3 and 7 score 21-22; books 4-6 score 18-21, pulled down by specific scene losses. Weighted synthesis lands at 21: main voice fully intact, secondary personality dimensions modestly but consistently reduced.

narrative_role_agency.book_baseline: Hagrid is a multi-function narrative agent across the series: herald and guide (PS), comic-dangerous secret-spiller (PS, CoS, HBP), emotional anchor (every book), creature-pedagogy subplot driver (PoA, GoF, OotP), plot catalyst through inadvertent disclosure (PS, CoS, HBP), active physical agent (PoA Azkaban scene, OotP centaur confrontation and arrest, DH flight), and diplomatic emissary (OotP giant mission). His agency is highest in books 3, 5, and 6 where he drives subplots independently.
narrative_role_agency.film_portrayal: Core herald and guide functions (PS), the dragon-showing agency (GoF), the spider-hint delivery (CoS), the Buckbeak defense participation (PoA), the Grawp introduction (OotP), the flight sequence (DH), and the body-carrying (DH) are all preserved. The films consistently retain Hagrid's most plot-critical single acts.
narrative_role_agency.difference: Consistent and significant losses across multiple books: the Three Broomsticks testimony (PoA, transferred to McGonagall and Fudge), the OotP giant mission diplomatic agency (compressed to a few lines), the centaur confrontation (OotP, removed entirely), the Snape/Dumbledore inadvertent disclosure (HBP, absent), the Karkaroff confrontation (GoF, absent), the HBP initiating letter to Harry (removed), and the sustained skrewt pedagogy subplot (GoF). In several books he is reduced from an active multi-function agent to a reactive supporting presence.
narrative_role_agency.evidence_status: Directly evidenced across all per-book analyses
narrative_role_agency.penalty_logic: Books 1, 2, and 7 preserve agency reasonably well (scores 15-17). Books 3, 4, 5, and 6 each show meaningful agency reductions (scores 13-15). The pattern is consistent: the films keep Hagrid's single most plot-critical act per book but remove the secondary agency functions that make him a genuine narrative driver. The OotP losses are the most severe - the giant mission, centaur confrontation, and arrest scene together strip out the book in which he has the most independent narrative weight. Weighted synthesis: 14.

motivations_internal_conflict.book_baseline: Hagrid's motivations are consistent across the series - loyalty to Dumbledore, love for Harry and the trio, creature obsession, pride in his Hogwarts role - but each book adds specific internal conflict: the shame of his expulsion (CoS, HBP), fear of Azkaban (PoA), the tension between creature-love and awareness of danger (PS, GoF), the fraternal love for Grawp overriding practical sense (OotP), and the wounded pride of professional rejection (HBP). The richest internal conflict is in PoA (fear of Azkaban vs. desire to save Buckbeak) and GoF (shame about half-giant heritage).
motivations_internal_conflict.film_portrayal: Core motivations (loyalty, protectiveness, creature love) are preserved in every film. The simpler motivational layer is consistently intact. Some specific conflict is preserved: the creature-love tension (PS Norbert arc, GoF dragon scene), the fraternal love-overriding-sense (OotP Grawp), the expulsion shame (implied by flashback in CoS).
motivations_internal_conflict.difference: The internal conflict dimension is consistently flattened. PoA: the Azkaban-fear motivation (the most psychologically revealing conflict in the series) is replaced by a simpler Dumbledore-loyalty motivation. GoF: the shame-spiral arc is compressed to a brief childhood monologue; the 'never be ashamed' resolution is absent. HBP: the secret-keeping vs. emotional incontinence conflict disappears. OotP: the tension between job anxiety and stubborn creature enthusiasm is reduced. The film Hagrid is consistently motivated but rarely conflicted.
motivations_internal_conflict.penalty_logic: Correct motivations throughout, but the internal conflict dimension - which is what elevates Hagrid from a warm supporting character to a psychologically coherent one - is consistently underserved. The PoA substitution is the most significant single change. Weighted synthesis: 12.

character_arc.book_baseline: Hagrid's overarching arc across the series is deliberately flat in terms of personality but rich in situation: he moves from gamekeeper-on-the-margins to teacher (PoA) to vulnerable public figure (GoF shame arc) to battered diplomatic emissary and endangered outsider (OotP) to grieving survivor (HBP, DH). Within each book, he has a distinct contained arc. The most developed are PoA (tentative hope to humiliation to unexpected relief), GoF (exposure, shame, recovery), and HBP (wounded pride to cumulative grief and resilient loyalty).
character_arc.film_portrayal: The broad situational arc across the series is legible in the films. The PoA arc's shape (excited teacher to arrested figure to vindication) is preserved. The DH situational arc (survivor under escalating danger) is intact. The GoF and HBP arcs are present as gestures rather than dramatized progressions.
character_arc.difference: The GoF shame-and-recovery arc is the most significant arc failure: the crisis (Skeeter article, public shame, retreat) and resolution ('never be ashamed', father's photograph, Dumbledore visit) are both absent, leaving only start and end states. The PoA arc loses its middle phase (flobberworm confidence collapse). The HBP arc loses its opening (sulking rejection) and closing (resilient loyalty declaration). The OotP arc loses its connective tissue (probation deterioration, distracted teaching). Across books, the films preserve arc endpoints but skip the intermediate stages that earn them.
character_arc.penalty_logic: No arc is entirely absent, but several are so compressed that their defining crises and turning points are missing. The GoF arc failure is the most complete. PoA and HBP arcs are structurally recognizable but incomplete. Books 1, 2, and 7 score better (13) because their arcs are simpler or intentionally flat. Weighted synthesis accounting for GoF and OotP failures: 12.

key_relationships.book_baseline: Hagrid's most important relationships across the series are: Harry (quasi-parental, the primary constant across all seven books), Dumbledore (near-devotional, Hagrid's emotional anchor and source of identity), the trio broadly (protective, mutually caring, occasionally critical), Aragog (creature-love at its most complex - mutual care despite danger), and Madame Maxime in GoF-OotP (romantic, humanizing, complicated by shared identity). Secondary: Ron's critical affection (CoS), Hermione's practical friction (OotP, HBP).
key_relationships.film_portrayal: Harry-Hagrid and Hagrid-Dumbledore relationships are consistently preserved in tone and function across the series. The Aragog relationship is preserved in CoS and HBP. The trio warmth is present throughout.
key_relationships.difference: Consistent losses: the Madame Maxime relationship loses its depth in GoF (shame/rejection/recovery) and is absent from OotP; Ron's critical-affective dimension is thin throughout; Hermione's practical friction (OotP, HBP) is reduced to uniform warmth. The Harry-Hagrid relationship loses its peacetime warmth dimension in DH (birthday scene, Hedwig comfort). The Dumbledore relationship loses the inadvertent-disclosure complexity in HBP. No relationship is entirely absent but all are somewhat flattened toward their warmest, simplest expression.
key_relationships.penalty_logic: The two primary relationships (Harry, Dumbledore) are functionally preserved in every film. The secondary relationships are consistently simplified. The Madame Maxime loss in GoF-OotP is the most significant individual relationship failure. Per-book scores range 7-8 with no book scoring higher. Synthesis: 7.

complexity_nuance_lost_material.book_baseline: Hagrid's complexity across the series derives from the gap between his idealized self-image and his actual behavior: he is brave and self-destructive, loyal and naively dangerous, warm and capable of wounded petty withdrawal, passionate and oblivious to consequences. The most complexity-bearing material is: the Azkaban confession (PoA), the flobberworm confidence collapse (PoA), the shame-arc and 'never be ashamed' resolution (GoF), the giant mission's strategic competence alongside naivety (OotP), the Madame Maxime romantic vulnerability (GoF-OotP), the Snape/Dumbledore inadvertent disclosure (HBP), and the sulking wounded-pride cycles (HBP, OotP). Cumulatively these establish a character who is psychologically marked, not just emotionally expressive.
complexity_nuance_lost_material.film_portrayal: The films preserve surface complexity well: guilelessness-as-flaw, creature obsession as self-destructive, emotional transparency, physical comedy coexisting with genuine heroism. Several high-fidelity complexity moments survive (betrayal monologue in DH, spider-hint under duress in CoS, Aragog burial blend of grief and guileless hospitality in HBP).
complexity_nuance_lost_material.difference: The Azkaban confession is the single greatest loss in the entire corpus - it is the only moment where Hagrid speaks about internal psychological experience and is irreplaceable in establishing him as psychologically marked rather than merely emotionally expressive. The GoF shame arc, the OotP giant mission depth, the HBP sulking-and-wit, the Madame Maxime complexity, and the flobberworm phase are all absent. Cumulatively the film Hagrid is a consistently warm, loyal, creature-obsessed figure whose rough edges (petty withdrawal, political naivety, physical violence in anger, xenophobic outburst, romantic vulnerability) are systematically removed.
complexity_nuance_lost_material.evidence_status: Directly evidenced across all per-book analyses
complexity_nuance_lost_material.penalty_logic: The pattern of simplification is consistent and cumulative. No single book reduces him to a cartoon, but the same secondary complexity layer is removed in book after book. The Azkaban confession alone would trigger a significant penalty; combined with the GoF shame arc, OotP mission depth, and HBP prickliness, the total loss of complexity is substantial. Per-book scores range 9-11. Synthesis: 10.

comparative.key_observations: Hagrid is one of the more faithfully adapted characters in the film series at the surface level - Robbie Coltrane's performance preserves dialect, warmth, emotional transparency, loyalty, and physical presence with consistent fidelity across all eight films. The core identity is never distorted or contradicted. The films always keep his single most plot-critical act per book. However, the adaptation exhibits a systematic pattern across all seven books: the warm, gentle, loyal dimensions of Hagrid are preserved while the rougher, more complicated dimensions are consistently cut. What accumulates across the series is the near-total loss of: his psychological depth (the Azkaban confession is irreplaceable), his capacity for petty wounded withdrawal and passive aggression, his political naivety and xenophobia, his physical violence in anger, his romantic vulnerability with Madame Maxime, and his inadvertent plot-driving through secret-spilling. The books' Hagrid is simultaneously the warmest adult in Harry's life and a genuinely flawed, self-destructive, oblivious figure whose creature-love creates real danger and whose judgment is often catastrophically poor. The films' Hagrid is primarily the former. He is not simplified to a single trait, but the contradictions that make him psychologically substantial are consistently resolved in favor of his most sympathetic register. Books 1, 2, and 7 are the most faithfully adapted; books 4, 5, and 6 show the steepest losses in arc, agency, and complexity. PoA is the critical case: the book in which Hagrid is most psychologically revealed is also the one where the most psychologically significant material is cut. The total of 76 reflects a portrayal that is recognizably and emotionally faithful but meaningfully simplified - a character whose warmth survives intact but whose weight does not.
